## App structure 

The call tree below is built with [`stackcallr`](https://mjfrigaard.github.io/stackcallr/). `call_tree_dir()` parses the files in `R/` without running them, and `modules_only = TRUE` keeps only the functions that call `NS()` or `moduleServer()`:

```{r}
#| label: app-structure
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("stackcallr", quietly = TRUE)
#| comment: ""
stackcallr::call_tree_dir("../R", root = "launch", modules_only = TRUE)
```

### React client

The UI is a React client built with [`shinyreact`](https://posit-dev.github.io/shinyreact/). The source is in `js/src/` and builds into `inst/www/ui.js` and `ui.css`, which `app_ui()` serves with `shinyreact::page_react()`. Each tab is wrapped in a `ShinyModuleProvider` whose namespace matches the module id in `app_server()`, so the server modules keep their ids. See `vignette("shinyreact-conversion")` for how each output type is hosted.

To rebuild the client after editing `js/src/`:

```bash
cd js
npm install
npm run build
```

### Variable inputs 

The dataset title input (`input$ds_title`) comes from the React client (`js/src/components/TitleInput.tsx`). `mod_input_server()` sends the client the list of titles (`output$titles`) and passes the selected title to `load_tt_data()`: 

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
tryCatch({
    result <- load_tt_data(title())
    if (length(result) == 0) {
      logr_msg("Empty dataset returned", level = "WARN")
      showNotification("No data available for selected dataset",
        type = "warning", duration = 5
      )
    } else {
      logr_msg("Dataset successfully loaded in reactive",
        level = "SUCCESS"
      )
    }
    return(result)
  },
  error = function(e) {
    logr_msg(paste("Error in data reactive:", e$message),
      level = "ERROR"
    )
    showNotification(paste("Error loading data:", e$message),
      type = "error", duration = 10
    )
    return(list())
  }
)
```

`mod_input_server()` returns a list with two reactives: the dataset list (`data`) and the title (`ds_title`).
```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
return(
    list(
      data = data,
      'ds_title' = reactive(input$ds_title)
    )
  )
```

In the `app_server()`, the inputs are assigned to the `title_input` and separated into `selected_data` and `dataset_title`:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
# initialize modules
title_input <- mod_input_server("input")
# return the data and title
selected_data <- title_input$data
dataset_title <- title_input$ds_title
```

These reactive values are passed to the output modules.

## List 

`mod_list` is a simple module that collects the list of `#TidyTuesday` datasets from the `mod_input_server()`: 

### Input Controls

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
# collect data
mod_list_server(id = "listviewerlite", data = selected_data)
```

### List Display

The list display comes from the [`listviewerlite` package](https://long39ng.github.io/listviewerlite/). The `mod_list_server()` accepts the `selected_data` as `data()` 

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
# render data()
output$list <- renderUI({
  req(data())
  listviewerlite::listview(data())
})
```

## Graphs

The `mod_plot` module draws `inspectdf` plots for one file at a time. The controls (a file dropdown and plot type checkboxes) live in the React client (`js/src/components/GraphsTab.tsx`); the server sends the choices and renders the plots.

### Input Controls

The client sends two inputs: `input$dataset` (the file) and `input$plots` (the checked plot types, `"types"`, `"mem"`, and `"na"` by default). The file names go the other way, from the server to the client, with `shinyreact::reactive_output()`:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
output$datasets <- shinyreact::reactive_output({
  if (is.null(ttd_r())) return(NULL)
  names(ttd_r())
})
```

When the file names change (a new title), the client selects the first file. `ttd_r()` is `ttd` itself when `ttd` is reactive, or `reactive(ttd)` when it is a static list, so the module works with either.

### Plot Display

The server defines one `renderPlot()` per plot type up front. Each one renders only while its type is checked, and the client shows an `ImageOutput` for each checked type:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
purrr::walk(PLOT_TYPES, function(plt) {
  output[[paste0("plt_", plt)]] <- renderPlot({
    req(plt %in% input$plots)
    ds <- selected() # outside tryCatch() so req() is not caught as an error
    tryCatch(
      inspect_plot(ttd = ds, plots = plt),
      error = function(err) {
        plot.new()
        text(0.5, 0.5, "Error generating plot", cex = 1.2, col = "red")
      }
    )
  })
})
```

`PLOT_TYPES` in `R/mod_plot.R` must match `PLOT_TYPES` in `GraphsTab.tsx`, which also holds the readable labels (Column types, Memory usage, Missing values, Correlations, Most common values, Numeric distributions, Categorical levels) used for the checkboxes and plot headings. The module returns a reactive list with the selected `dataset` and `plots`.

#### inspect_plot()

`inspect_plot()` uses the `inspectdf` package to draw seven kinds of plot:

* `"types"`: column type distributions
* `"mem"`: memory usage
* `"na"`: missing value patterns
* `"cor"`: correlations
* `"imb"`: feature imbalance for categorical data
* `"num"`: numeric column summaries
* `"cat"`: categorical column summaries

In `app_server()`, the module gets the loaded data:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
title_input <- mod_input_server("input")
selected_data <- title_input$data
mod_plot_server("viz", ttd = selected_data)
```

### Error Handling

`req()` stops a plot until its inputs are valid. `tryCatch()` replaces a failed plot with a placeholder, and `logr_msg()` logs the error.

## Summary

The Summary tab (`mod_summary_server()` and `js/src/components/SummaryTab.tsx`) lists each file with its rows and columns. For the file picked in its dropdown, it shows three `reactable` tables:

* Summary statistics: rows, columns, missing values, complete rows, and data types, from `tt_file_summary()`.
* Variable information: one row per column with its type, missing count, missing percent, and unique values, from `tt_var_info()`. Missing percents over 10 are shaded yellow; over 50, red.
* Data: the file itself in a searchable, sortable, paged table. Only the first 1,000 rows are shown to keep the browser responsive; the sidebar download has the full file.

## Download

The sidebar download (`mod_download_server()` and `js/src/components/Download.tsx`) saves the loaded data in one of three formats:

| Format | What is written |
|---|---|
| CSV | each data frame written with `vroom::vroom_write()` |
| Parquet | each data frame written with `nanoparquet::write_parquet()` |
| Original format | each file fetched again from its `github_url` attribute (set by `load_tt_data()`) |

A title with one file downloads that file. A title with several files downloads one `.zip` named after the title and format (for example, `lego_database_csv.zip`). The internal helpers `tt_download_filename()` and `write_tt_download()` pick the name and write the file:

```{r}
#| label: download-example
#| eval: false
ttd <- load_tt_data("Space Launches")
ttdviewer:::tt_download_filename(ttd, "parquet", "Space Launches")
ttdviewer:::write_tt_download(ttd, "parquet", file = "space_launches_parquet.zip")
```
